A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same reflection-removal system. Their text, equations, tables, figures and complete supplementary materials support reliable comparison despite substantial reformatting.

before.justification: V1 reports original synthetic-data evaluations in Tables 1–2, real-photograph comparisons, ablations and supplementary failure analyses.

after.justification: V2 retains these original evaluations and adds DSRNet comparisons, a reflection-as-context ablation, travel examples and reflection-editing demonstrations.

M1.justification: The reflection simulator, context-modulated base model, feature-mask upsampler, losses and inference pipeline are retained. V2's color-processing pseudocode and backbone specifications document existing procedures; they do not establish a changed algorithm or architecture.

E1.justification: V2 adds two travel photographs in Fig. A5 and exercises aesthetic editing and error correction in Sec. 5.4 and Appendix F.4. MIT5K, RAISE, Laval Indoors and the three original ground-truth capture scenarios remain unchanged. Fig. A5 also reuses the scene from v1 Fig. 7.

E2.justification: V2 substantially revises the central comparisons by adding DSRNet to Table 1 and replacing CoRRN with DSRNet throughout the matched visual comparisons, including retrained and published 8-bit models. CoRRN remains in Table 1. Zhang and the V-DESIRR upsampling comparisons are retained.

E3.justification: V2 introduces a test-time control that substitutes the ground-truth reflection for context, c = r, and a photographer editing procedure. Existing splits, training budgets, resolutions and metric procedures remain unchanged. Expanded preprocessing specifications document existing experiments rather than establish revised settings.

E4.justification: The new c = r ablation tests whether perfectly matching reflection content improves contextual inference. V2 also adds editing case studies demonstrating aesthetic control and correction of removed object reflections. The random-context and upsampler-mask ablations, lens-flare example and existing failure analyses are retained.

E5.justification: The significance bounds in Tables 1–2 remain p < 1.7e-11 and p < 1e-12. Neither version supplies repeated-run counts, seeds or confidence intervals, and v2 introduces no new uncertainty-reporting or statistical-testing procedure.

E6.justification: V2 adds DSRNet transmission/reflection PSNRs of 28.98/23.99 and reflection-as-context PSNRs of 33.20/30.20 in Table 1. Numerous CoRRN visual outputs and SSIM entries are replaced by DSRNet results, alongside new travel and editing results. These are new comparisons, not same-method performance gains. Most retained scores only change precision, although Table 2's control reflection PSNR changes from 13.153 to 13.13.

T1.justification: The mixture relations, Fresnel attenuation equations, defocus and double-reflection derivations, and loss formulas are retained. Added color-transform pseudocode elaborates implementation without introducing a new theoretical result or substantively revising the existing mathematical reasoning.

C1.justification: Both versions retain the four contributions: accurate synthetic training, contextual disambiguation, approximately five-second previews and full-resolution reflection removal. V2's additional comparisons and editing demonstrations support these existing claims. The MacBook timing newly highlighted in its abstract already appears in v1 Sec. 5.3.

C2.justification: V2 adds interpretations linking contextual gains to image content and robustness to disjoint-crop training, using the random-context and c = r comparisons. It also discusses color-matrix precision under extreme lighting and recommends linear-RGB blending for realistic edits. Existing limitations involving nighttime scenes, saturation and overlapping textures remain.

D1.justification: Sec. 3 and new Appendices A/G substantially expand reproducibility information through simulation pseudocode, DNG SDK 1.7.1 functions, color-matrix conversion, exposure targets, C5's seven camera samples, white-balance filtering and black-level/highlight handling. Appendix E.1 specifies EfficientNet-B1/EfficientDet-D0, stride and pooling details; Appendix D.3 adds the camera-ray rejection threshold. These are newly documented details, not demonstrated implementation changes.

R1.justification: V2 adds references including CIE XYZ Net, RAW unprocessing and camera-pipeline work, DSRNet, and Zhu et al. It expands discussion of real-dataset scale and pretraining, and removes v1's argument about Zhang–CoRRN rankings contradicting earlier evaluations. The central positioning around accurate RAW simulation and consumer photography remains.

P1.justification: The main section sequence and much of the prose are retained. V2 expands the color-processing explanation, introduces dedicated editing and SDK sections, reorganizes supplementary headings into lettered appendices, renames the shuffled-context condition and makes local wording and attribution corrections.

P2.justification: V2 replaces the two-column presentation with a single-column layout, adds numerous pseudocode boxes and new editing/travel displays, and restructures Table 1 into comparison and ablation groups. The base-model diagram moves from v1 Fig. 10 into main-text Fig. 2, and existing photographic comparisons are redistributed and revised with DSRNet panels.

improvement.justification: V1 leaves important details of pre-white-balance RAW conversion and C5 integration unspecified. V2's Sec. 3 and Appendices A/G supply the color-matrix path, exposure/white-balance procedures and SDK details, substantially improving reproducibility of the central synthetic-data contribution. DSRNet comparisons and the c = r control strengthen validation, while editing demonstrations substantiate previously asserted practical utility. These gains are substantial despite largely unchanged retained model scores.
